summary: A round must end in an end face that is not square to its edge, along that face's section of the round (#215). A prism on a trapezoid, 10 high, has the top edge along y = 0 rounded r 2; one end face is square, the other leans in (far 30) or out (far 50). The removed section's length at depth y into the top face is 40 + (far - 40) y / 20, linear, so the removed volume is the section's area times the length at its centroid: closed form. SolidCraft checked 2e-4 relative on a mesh; these check 1e-4 mm^3. The test's chamfer-mitre case (a Monte Carlo estimate) is not ported.

cases.name: end_face_at_an_angle_far_30
cases.note: Prism on the trapezoid (0,0) (40,0) (30,20) (0,20), 10 high; the top edge along y = 0 rounded r 2. It ends square at x = 0 and in the face through (40,0) and (30,20) at an angle.

removed.formula: (1 - pi/4)*2^2 * (40 + (30 - 40)*c/20), c = 2*(10 - 3*pi)/(3*(4 - pi)) (the section's length is linear in its depth y, so its mean is the length at the centroid)

cases.name: end_face_at_an_angle_far_50
cases.note: Prism on the trapezoid (0,0) (40,0) (50,20) (0,20), 10 high; the top edge along y = 0 rounded r 2. It ends square at x = 0 and in the face through (40,0) and (50,20) at an angle.

removed.formula: (1 - pi/4)*2^2 * (40 + (50 - 40)*c/20), c = 2*(10 - 3*pi)/(3*(4 - pi)) (the section's length is linear in its depth y, so its mean is the length at the centroid)
